newsitem.title: LATVIA: LETA NEWS AGENCY FACES LAST REVIVAL ATTEMPT.
newsitem.headline: LETA NEWS AGENCY FACES LAST REVIVAL ATTEMPT.

text.p: The privatisation agency said on Wednesday that it has turned LETA, the domestic state-owned news agency, into a state limited company in a last attempt to revive the insolvent company.
LETA was set up at the beginning of the 1920s as Latvia's voice when the country first gained its independence.

"This is an attempt to inject some money into the agency and then find an investor who could bring it back to life," Arvis Freibergs, head of the privatisation agency's audit department, told a news conference.
"The agency has had its telephones and faxes cut off for non-payment of bills but its main asset is still its building in the Old Town," he added.
The agency said the rules to attract some fresh capital would be ready in a month.
"If the plan fails, there is only one way -- bankruptcy," Freibergs said.
